lines: Look closely at your microwave door. See all those tiny holes?
That metal mesh is a shield.
Uh oh. Did anyone else just lose their Wi-Fi?
Microwaves and Wi-Fi use almost the same frequency.
Without the mesh, those waves pour straight out of the door. The same waves that heat your food.
They make water molecules wiggle... including the water in you.
So how can tiny holes stop them? Microwaves are about [12|twelve] centimeters long.
The holes are only a millimeter or two. The waves are way too big to squeeze through. But light? Light fits easily.
Fun fact: in [1945|nineteen forty-five], engineer Percy Spencer was working near radar equipment, and the candy bar in his pocket melted.
The first microwave oven was almost six feet tall!
So that boring little mesh? It lets you watch your popcorn without cooking yourself.
So... what should I delete next?
